dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning the repo and running node marketing_hub.js with commands like analyze/titles/script. The runtime JS only reads/writes files under scripts/ (memory files) and calls external APIs; however it also launches system processes (Chrome, Xvfb, pkill, ffmpeg, whisper) for browser scraping and media tasks. The instructions do not ask for unrelated secrets or data exfiltration; data is stored locally in scripts/memory/*.json as described.

The manifest/file permissions are slightly broader than the code requires: write access to ${WORKSPACE_ROOT} is declared even though code writes to scripts/memory. This grants more filesystem write scope than appears necessary.

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not modify other skills, which is good. However the code executes system-level commands (execSync/exec), can start/kill Xvfb, and the manifest explicitly allows pkill and many subprocess patterns. Those subprocess permissions and pkill usage could affect other processes on the host if run with elevated privileges — run in a sandbox and avoid running as root.

llm.guidance: This skill's behavior generally matches its description (it fetches Douyin data via TikHub and uses DeepSeek for AI). Before installing: 1) Inspect the included scripts locally (marketing_hub.js) and confirm you are comfortable with it running child processes (Chrome/Xvfb/ffmpeg/whisper) and creating files under the skill directory. 2) Do not provide high-privilege or long-lived credentials — use limited/test API keys. 3) Run the skill in an isolated environment (container/VM) because it may start/kill X server processes and calls pkill. 4) If you won't use browser scraping or audio features, avoid running those modes and do not install optional system tools (ffmpeg/whisper/chrome). 5) Consider removing or restricting the manifest's ${WORKSPACE_ROOT} write permission if you manage the skill bundle yourself.
